name: What if I only remodel the kitchen and bathrooms but call it a whole-house remodel?

mainEntity.name: Does updating only a few rooms count as a whole-house remodel, or is that something else?
mainEntity.text: Does updating only a few rooms count as a whole-house remodel, or is that something else?

acceptedAnswer.text: Updating only the kitchen and bathrooms is usually considered a partial remodel, even if the work is extensive and expensive. A true whole-house remodel typically affects most of the main living areas and often includes flooring throughout, lighting, paint, doors, windows, and sometimes plumbing, electrical, or HVAC upgrades. The distinction matters because pricing, timeline, and contractor scope change significantly depending on how much of the home is included. A partial remodel can still deliver a major transformation, but it will not usually address layout consistency, whole-home material continuity, or system-wide modernization. Homeowners should define the project honestly before requesting bids. That helps contractors price the work correctly and prevents confusion when comparing estimates from different firms. Clear terminology also makes it easier to decide whether a broader renovation would be more efficient in the long run.
